name: Python in Depth
audience: Experienced developers who already write Python and want to understand how it really works: the object model, the interpreter, concurrency and modern typing.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of code-reading, predict-the-output, debugging and design questions.
scenarios: Speeding up a slow data pipeline
Moving a sync service to asyncio
verifyNotes: This is the site's own deep-foundations course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources). Goal: the learner can explain and reason about every idea confidently in a senior interview or design review. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise definition or mechanism, then a fully worked example, then where it matters in real systems (including AI/ML and LLM application code where natural), then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally). In JSON strings escape backslashes (\\log). Code in fenced ```python blocks that run as-is. Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small Python exercise with the expected output. Verifiers MUST run every compute and code-output question with {{root}}/.pipeline/py313/bin/python (CPython 3.13, standard library only) and fix keys that disagree; state any randomness seed in the stem; never depend on dict/set ordering that Python does not guarantee, or on id() values. Question mix: ~35% concept/judgment, ~40% predict-the-output or behaviour of a snippet, ~25% debug-or-choose-the-right-approach. Target Python 3.13 (note when a feature is 3.12+ or 3.13+, e.g. type-parameter syntax, free-threaded build, the new REPL) and say CPython when behaviour is an implementation detail (refcounting, small-int caching, bytecode). Bytecode questions: ask about concepts, not exact opcode listings, which change between versions. Sources: docs.python.org (reference, library, howto, glossary, whatsnew), peps.python.org and the CPython devguide only; no blogs or Medium.

domains.name: The data model and object system
skills: Special methods and protocols: __repr__, __eq__/__hash__ contract, rich comparison, container and numeric protocols, __bool__ and __len__
Attribute lookup: instance and class dicts, __getattr__ vs __getattribute__, descriptors, property, __slots__
Inheritance: MRO and C3 linearization, cooperative super(), mixins and abstract base classes
Class creation: type, metaclasses, __init_subclass__, __set_name__, class decorators, and when to use each
Callables and object identity: bound methods, staticmethod/classmethod, is vs ==, interning and caching as CPython details

domains.name: Functions, scopes, iterators and generators
skills: Scopes: LEGB, closures and late binding, global and nonlocal, default-argument evaluation
Decorators: functools.wraps, decorators with arguments, stacking order, decorating methods
The iterator protocol, iterables vs iterators, generators, yield from, send/throw/close
Lazy pipelines with itertools and generator expressions; memory and laziness trade-offs
functools: partial, lru_cache/cache, singledispatch, reduce; first-class functions

domains.name: Memory, the interpreter and the import system
skills: Names, references and mutability: aliasing, shallow vs deep copy, argument passing
Memory management in CPython: reference counting, the cyclic garbage collector, weakref, __del__ pitfalls, finding leaks with tracemalloc
How code runs: compilation to bytecode, code objects and frames, the dis module at a conceptual level
The GIL, what it does and does not protect, and the free-threaded build (PEP 703) in 3.13+
The import system: modules, packages, sys.path, finders and loaders, circular imports, __main__

domains.name: Concurrency and asyncio
skills: Choosing threads, processes or asyncio for I/O-bound vs CPU-bound work; concurrent.futures
asyncio fundamentals: coroutines, the event loop, tasks, await, gather vs TaskGroup
Cancellation, timeouts (asyncio.timeout), exception groups and except*
Common async bugs: blocking calls in the loop, forgotten awaits, unbounded concurrency; semaphores and to_thread
Thread safety: races, locks, queues, and what is atomic in CPython

domains.name: Modern typing and language features
skills: Type hints and static checking: generics, TypeVar and 3.12 type-parameter syntax, variance at a working level
Structural typing with Protocol; TypedDict, Literal, overload, Self, ParamSpec
dataclasses in depth: field defaults, frozen, slots, __post_init__, ordering; vs NamedTuple and attrs-style classes
Structural pattern matching (match/case): patterns, guards and pitfalls
Enums, context managers (contextlib) and exception design

domains.name: Performance, testing and packaging
skills: Cost model of built-ins: list, dict, set and deque operation complexity; string building
Measuring: timeit, cProfile, tracemalloc; optimizing hot paths without guessing
Testing with pytest: fixtures, parametrize, mocking with unittest.mock, testing async code
Packaging: pyproject.toml, virtual environments, entry points, version pinning
Writing a clean public API: __all__, keyword-only arguments, deprecation, documentation
